newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West peak spot power higher amid cold snap.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West peak spot power higher amid cold snap.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West, particulary during peak hours, moved up as high demand due to cold weather in the Northwest helped offset slightly weaker natural gas prices, market sources said Wednesday.

In addition, the unplanned outage of a 700 megawatt (MW) unit at the Colstrip coal-fired plant in Montana and a delay in the restart of a 720 MW unit at the Navajo power plant in Arizona were cited as adding to market tightness.
Traders noted that incremental power from natural gas-fired units continues to set the benchmark for cash prices.
"With spot natgas around $4.00 (per million British thermal units) or more, we could clearly get up to around $60 (per megawatt hour) without much effort," said one California trader.
Firm, peak electricity at COB on Thursday was quoted $40.00-50.00 per MWh, compared with $30.00-33.00 for Wednesday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Thursday was quoted near $21.00, compared with around $20.00 on Tuesday.
Thursday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was pegged at $45.00-$55.00, compared with $32.00-36.00 Tuesday.
COB for first quarter 1997 was quoted $21.00-22.00, while second quarter was assessed near $14.50 and third quarter was quoted $21.00-21.50.
First quarter Palo Verde was quoted $22.50-23.00, while second quarter was pegged at $18.00-18.50 and third quarter was at $25.00-25.40.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Thursday was quoted $45.00-50.00, compared with $29.50-30.50.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Thursday was quoted near $16.00-$17.00.
Thursday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were in line with PV at around $45.00. Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was assessed at $15.50-$16.50.
